Poisson cutoff estimator of CFU

find_poisson_cutoff.Rd

Pools all observations with counts below N (counts at or above N are distrusted) and estimates the rate as total count divided by total dilution times volume.

Usage

find_poisson_cutoff(counts, dil, N = 300, V = 1)

Arguments

counts

Numeric vector of colony counts.

dil

Numeric vector of dilution factors (e.g. 1e-5), same length as counts.

N

Counts greater than or equal to N are excluded. Defaults to 300, the value recommended for 100 mm petri dishes. Use Inf to keep all counts (naive Poisson estimate).

V

Sampling volume. The default of 1 returns absolute CFU in the amount plated or spotted.

Value

A one-row data frame with columns r, stderr and type. r is NA if no observations fall below N.

Details

Setting N = Inf excludes nothing and gives the naive Poisson estimate, which pools every observation.

Examples

counts <- c(2, 4, 3, 25, 32)
dil <- c(1e-6, 1e-6, 1e-6, 1e-5, 1e-5)
find_poisson_cutoff(counts, dil, N = 30)
#>         r   stderr           type
#> 1 2615385 448534.8 poisson_cutoff

# No cutoff: naive Poisson estimate
find_poisson_cutoff(counts, dil, N = Inf)
#>         r   stderr           type
#> 1 2869565 353219.1 poisson_cutoff
